items.title: What are tariffs, and how do they work?
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore how tariffs work and dig into how their enactment can set off an economic chain reaction that impacts global trade.

--

In 1930, in hopes of supporting farms and manufacturing, President Hoover made a bold decision: he approved a sweeping 20% tax on all imported agricultural and industrial goods. But the plan completely backfired, leading exports to fall and global trade to decline. And it wouldn't be the last time a world leader was shocked by a tariff’s consequences. Trace the economic chain reaction of tariffs.

Directed by Avi Ofer.

items.title: 4 ways to tell a great story
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Episode 7: Discover the 4 components of what makes a great storyteller, and the important role that stories play in audience connection.

--

This is episode 7 of the animated series, “Public Speaking 101.” Ideas change everything — and since language lets us share our ideas, learning how to use it well gives speakers the power to inspire people and even change how they think. This 11-episode course will teach you how to identify, develop, and share your best ideas, while mastering essential communication skills along the way.

Directed by Tolga Yıldız, Kozmonot Animation Studio.

The TED-Ed Student Talks program provides free, customizable activities for educators to support their students in identifying, developing and sharing their ideas with each other and the world. Learn more at https://ed.ted.com/student_talks

items.title: Plato’s infamous Ship of State thought experiment - Michael Vazquez
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into Plato’s infamous Ship of State thought experiment, which explores how democratic societies handle leadership and power.

--

Imagine a ship struggling in an endless storm. Its captain, though strong and commanding, is a terrible navigator. Neither he nor his crew have been trained to sail, yet they tirelessly vie for control through bribery, flattery, and mutiny, and ignore those with real navigation knowledge. This dysfunctional vessel is Plato's Ship of State. Michael Vazquez explores the infamous thought experiment.

Lesson by Michael Vazquez, directed by Luis Torres, Mr. Flama.

This video was produced in collaboration with the Parr Center for Ethics, housed within the renowned Philosophy Department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The Parr Center is committed to integrating abstract work in ethical theory with the informed discussion of practical ethical issues, and prides itself on the development of innovative and inclusive approaches to moral and civic education.

items.title: The tragedy of Cassandra, the princess who predicted the fall of Troy - Iseult Gillespie
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the Greek tragedy of Cassandra, who received the gift of prophecy but was cursed by Apollo to never be believed.

--

As a young woman, Cassandra of Troy had been pursued by the god Apollo, who offered her the gift of prophecy. But when she withdrew from his advances, he twisted his gift into a maddening hex: from that day on, Cassandra would be able to precisely see and describe the future— but her prophecies would never be believed. Iseult Gillespie details the Greek tragedy of the cursed seer.

Lesson by Iseult Gillespie, directed by Yael Reisfeld.

items.title: How do Maglev trains work? - Ning Zhao
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Learn more at https://brilliant.org/TedEd

--

To coincide with the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, Japan launched a groundbreaking bullet train that inspired countries around the world to invest in high-speed rail. Today, high-speed trains regularly travel at over 300 km/h, on par with the take-off speed of a commercial airplane. But can it ever be faster than flying? Ning Zhao details the possibilities and hurdles facing high-speed rail transit.

Lesson by Ning Zhao, directed by Vicente Numpaque, Dr3i Studio, Hernando Bahamon, Globizco Studios.
